from_speaker: could ever work at a profit

our_interpretation: In context, commercial product means a driverless transport service.
The claim asserts that needing remote help every few miles prevents profitable operation. It is stronger than saying Cruise was losing money.
Profit ordinarily means service revenue exceeding its full operating costs. Marcus specifies neither an accounting basis nor how shared development costs should be allocated.
Assistance frequency, assistance duration, and employees per vehicle are different measures.
criteria.support_condition: Operating evidence establishes that necessary assistance at approximately the reported frequency makes full service costs exceed achievable revenue across the claimed scope.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A commercial driverless service earns a documented operating profit while requiring remote human assistance approximately every few miles, with matching financial and assistance measurement periods.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A documented operating profit for a commercial driverless service requiring necessary remote assistance approximately every few miles, with financial and operational records covering the same period, would contradict the claim.
